title: [#112] Route MIDI by fixed track, port, channel and type
body:
When UI selection changes, generic MIDI previously followed the selected track and there was no explicit external output routing. This layer gives each track profile-owned input ports/channel masks/type filters and an exact external port/channel, while retaining legacy defaults.

Two controllers can now monitor separate tracks and address separate channels on one multitimbral output. Notes retain both velocities; CC/bank/program, both pressures, bend and opt-in complete bounded SysEx preserve wire bytes. Source clip output preserves channels/source order/ticks with the conductor. Preferences Preview/Cancel/save/reopen, routing receipts/retry/cancel, activity and explicit reset use the shipped UI.

Known configured/active input/output device overlap is refused. Output discovery/send/teardown stays on a dedicated worker; source/clip note and sustain ownership, stale generation/epoch rejection, queue/block bounds and reset refusal prevent obsolete onsets and stuck shared gates. Missing/ambiguous destinations never select a fallback. IPC retains its 8 KiB limit through a compact summary and explicit display-label truncation; detailed native names/activity remain available.

Addresses #112. Stacked on #467 / `stack/issue-111-smf-interchange`. Review the three commits and [supported behavior, failures and frozen evidence](docs/validation/issue-112-midi-routing.md).

Validation on local Linux aarch64:

- Full suite: 1,176 passed, zero failed, 26 opt-in ignored; 233.21 s.
- Unchanged standard gate: eight workloads × three repeats pass, original four audio hashes unchanged, callback heap zero.
- Private native accessibility: 158 actions, 246 visited nodes, 555 frames.
- Frozen release binary tests: two private ALSA source ports and one receiver deliver all 12 expected remapped packets plus resets; all private ports retired. Both native routing profile and missing-output/reset UI workflows pass. Actual renderer emits every fixture gate/controller/program at independently calculated frames at 48/96 kHz.
- Immutable package, license/source inventory, actual packaged CLI/follow/runtime-isolation/safe-start checks pass. Qualified source `702fa8bf7993c69aa0b753423e613ac600a72004`; final head adds qualification documentation only.

Supported boundaries: external output is source MIDI before internal arp/audio mixing, delivered asynchronously without calibrated hardware latency. SysEx is opaque, complete 3–256-byte packets with valid extended-id width; larger/fragmented packets refuse. Physical cable/thru topology cannot be inferred from packet equality; no blind repeated-packet filter is used. Rescan is explicit. Concurrent notes/sustain share ownership, while other controls on a shared channel follow arrival order.

Physical controller/multitimbral, listening, Orca and backend XRUN QA remain for the user's final producer/composer/live-DJ run. Private virtual traces are software evidence. The inherited issue #107 supplemental wall-max failures remain unresolved. No issue closure, merge, or installation over the active application is requested.

They assert snapshots match the cleared state, the new playhead starts at zero and advances through short media to its normal end, and the other deck remains unchanged. No hardware or listening test is claimed.

title: fix: bound and measure queued command work per audio block
body:
A continuously refilled command channel could keep the audio callback draining indefinitely. Limit each block to 32 received commands, including coalesced updates, using fixed stack storage. Coalesce only adjacent absolute assignments to the same parameter; preserve transport, note/pad gates, relative movements and target changes in FIFO order. Publish backlog, high-water, coalescing and budget-exhaustion metrics through the snapshot and CLI status.

Closes #5. Stacked on #360; review against `stack/issue-4-clip-voice-release`.

Validation: fresh local `cargo test --locked` passes 34 tests. Deterministic full-queue tests verify all eight batches and an on/off pair spanning a callback boundary. A synchronized concurrent producer submits 8,193 events into a saturated queue; the real renderer accounts for every event, obeys the per-block budget, advances audio and receives the final note-off through the queue without a direct rescue command. Generous liveness guards catch stalls; observed times are not device-deadline guarantees.

This bounds command count, not arbitrary individual handler cost. GUI admission/critical-event overload policy and MIDI callback blocking remain #11/#39. Details: `docs/validation/issue-5-command-budget.md`.

title: fix: release clip-owned voices across playback transitions
body:
Stopping or replacing a clip could leave its synth voices sustaining indefinitely. Tag live and clip voices separately and release clip-owned envelopes through a shared lifecycle path, including scene/track/transport stops, clip replacement, one-shot completion and note replacement. Same-pitch live notes keep their own gates; finite drum and effect tails retain their documented policy. Arp gates and cached chords reset with clip ownership.

Closes #4. Stacked on #359; review against `stack/issue-3-arp-cache`.

Validation: fresh local `cargo test --locked` passes all 30 tests. New regressions cover 12 stop/replacement paths with and without arp, same-pitch ownership in both trigger orders, reassignment after voice stealing, one-shot completion, other-track preservation and natural drum tails. Sustained clip voices enter release and finish within the configured envelope time while live notes remain held. No physical-controller or audio-device qualification is claimed.

title: fix: cache arpeggiator chords without per-sample allocation
body:
Arpeggiated clips rebuilt, sorted and allocated a chord vector every sample. Cache ordered chord membership in fixed storage and refresh at note boundaries, loop starts, edits and arp activation. Rest/removal releases the current gate; muted/solo-masked loop transitions invalidate stale chords. Borrow FX controls in place so an active arp slot does not reintroduce per-sample allocation.

Closes #3. Stacked on #358; review this branch against `stack/issue-2-scene-index`.

Validation: local `cargo test --locked` passes 25 tests. Allocation instrumentation reports zero allocations and frees for a real 1024-frame process block and 576,000 arpeggiated renderer frames spanning three loops, plus the first render after edits. Sequence/rest/loop/edit/enable/mute/solo tests pass. The FX borrowing prerequisite produced bit-identical output to the original implementation over 400,000 comparison frames; evidence and reproduction commands are in `docs/evidence/issue-3-arp.md`.

The allocation claim covers arpeggiator playback. Periodic snapshot construction remains separately tracked; these checks do not qualify live-device latency or hardware performance.

title: fix: reject invalid scene indexes at all control boundaries
body:
`omatainer ctl scene 9` could abort the process, and invalid scene commands could alter an unrelated active clip. Validate one-based CLI arguments, zero-based IPC types/ranges before narrowing, and all engine scene entry points before mutation. Invalid IPC scene requests return an explicit error; all eight valid scenes retain their behavior.

Closes #2. First layer of the ordered #1 backlog; base is `main`.

Validation: fresh local `cargo test --locked` passes 17 tests. `scripts/check-scene-inputs.py` passes the same CLI, IPC and engine regressions in a compile-checked `panic=abort` subprocess with core dumps disabled. Coverage includes every invalid u8 scene index, larger selection indexes, missing/negative/nonnumeric/wrong-type arguments, wraparound values and valid endpoints. No live application, audio device or physical controller was used. General malformed-JSON/unknown-op handling remains tracked in #28.

- [ ] Define and label render CPU, callback elapsed time and deadline overruns separately.
- [ ] Total callback telemetry includes command handoff, render, conversion and publication overhead.
- [ ] Metrics report dropped/late buffers without allocating or blocking in the callback.

**Validation**

<!-- omatainer-professional-backlog: fix-arp-chord-per-sample -->
**Priority:** P1 · **Area:** audio · **Tracking:** #1

The arpeggiator builds, sorts and deduplicates a chord Vec for every sample even though its sequence advances only at sixteenth-note boundaries. Arp itself is implemented; the defect is redundant real-time work.

**Evidence and scope**

- docs/evidence/audio-results.txt records 3072 allocations for one 1024-frame arpeggiated clip block, including note and FX clones.
- https://github.com/michaelmonetized/omatainer/blob/cae546c7bc840ec1a643e4befe18f91e86d0e4c7/src/engine/mod.rs#L765-L795

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Chord membership and order are recomputed only when note membership, clip edits or arp controls require it.
- [ ] Arpeggiated playback has zero steady-state heap allocations.
- [ ] Held chords, rests and loop boundaries retain correct note-offs and sequence order.

**Validation**

Instrument allocations while playing the existing chord fixture and compare emitted notes over several loops; include edits between arp steps.

Baseline: Omatainer `cae546c7bc840ec1a643e4befe18f91e86d0e4c7`; professional-capability review dated 2026-09-30. This issue is planned work, not a claim of shipped functionality.

<!-- omatainer-professional-backlog: fix-scene-index-abort -->
**Priority:** P0 · **Area:** integration · **Tracking:** #1

ctl scene 9 becomes zero-based scene 8, IPC accepts it, and LaunchScene indexes an eight-element clip array without validation. AddScene has the same unchecked pattern. A release-style isolated harness confirms SIGABRT because panic=abort.

**Evidence and scope**

- docs/evidence/integration-results.txt records scene 9 panic and isolated panic=abort return code -6; no desktop process was crashed.
- https://github.com/michaelmonetized/omatainer/blob/cae546c7bc840ec1a643e4befe18f91e86d0e4c7/src/main.rs#L101-L105
- https://github.com/michaelmonetized/omatainer/blob/cae546c7bc840ec1a643e4befe18f91e86d0e4c7/src/main.rs#L178-L180
- https://github.com/michaelmonetized/omatainer/blob/cae546c7bc840ec1a643e4befe18f91e86d0e4c7/src/engine/mod.rs#L1058-L1066
- https://github.com/michaelmonetized/omatainer/blob/cae546c7bc840ec1a643e4befe18f91e86d0e4c7/src/engine/mod.rs#L1471-L1478
- https://github.com/michaelmonetized/omatainer/blob/cae546c7bc840ec1a643e4befe18f91e86d0e4c7/Cargo.toml#L31-L34

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] CLI accepts only documented one-based scene indexes and rejects missing/invalid arguments explicitly.
- [ ] IPC validates types/ranges before conversion and engine scene operations defensively reject every invalid index.
- [ ] Malformed input never panics, aborts, mutates a different scene or reports success.
- [ ] Regression tests exercise every scene entry point including ToggleScene/RestartScene/AddScene.

**Validation**

Reuse integration scene tests with 0,9,255,256,negative,missing and nonnumeric values; test release panic strategy only in isolated processes with core dumps disabled.

Live 12.4.15b5 and [Serato 5.0 public beta](https://the-drop.serato.com/announcements/introducing-lucid-beatgrids-in-serato-dj-5-0/) are distinguished from released functionality.

P0 protects audio continuity, creative work and foundational operation. P1 covers essential professional workflows. P2 expands specialist workflows and ecosystem depth. P3 covers optional, platform-dependent or advanced capabilities. These priorities are sequencing proposals, not permission to omit scope.

This is a broad, versioned coverage inventory, not a claim that every specialist has identical needs or that Omatainer already implements parity. Beyond-baseline capabilities are identified in their issues. Proprietary products/assets are comparison references; equivalent original or licensed implementation is expected. Streaming, hardware, SDK and format integrations must confirm actual support and rights.
